newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MAS says to benefit from open skies agreement.
newsitem.headline: MAS says to benefit from open skies agreement.

text.p: Malaysia's national carrier, Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Sunday that the "open skies" agreement between United States and Malaysia would benefit the airline.
"MAS is very well positioned to take advantage of the open skies agreement," said MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli. "It will definitely improve our profits."
Malaysian Transport Minister said last week that the United States and Malaysia have agreed on an "open skies" treaty liberalising air travel between the countries.
The agreement would provide for unlimited landings and intermediate points to continue flights to other countries, Ling said.
Tajudin said MAS was looking for other airlines to operate along the east coast of the United States as its capacity at present could not cover the U.S. market as a whole.
"We are looking at two options on whether to go direct or code-sharing," he told reporters after witnessing the arrival of MAS's first Boeing 777-200.
